messages:
Nikhil (sec-eng): Heads-up: I'm starting a short sync on audit coverage & schema changes for org-facing exports. Need clarity on which fields are customer-visible vs internal for RBAC and scoped tokens.
Maria (product): thanks. what's the high-level ask? are we changing event shapes or just access rules?
Nikhil (sec-eng): both. customers asked for richer "actor" metadata in exports but we can't leak service-internal IDs. also want to support per-org admin vs member views.
Alex (eng-platform): quick note: we already have two flavors in the pipeline — export_v1 (internal) and export_public_v1. Are we proposing a new public schema or schema tags?
Nikhil (sec-eng): propose schema with 3 tiers: full_internal, org_admin_view, org_member_view. validation rules + transform step before export.
Chris (eng-sre): +1 for transform. operationally we can run transform in the audit-pipeline worker; adds ~60ms per batch. fine if batched.
Maria (product): what's the list of fields that get redacted for member_view? e.g., API keys, internal_user_ids, hostnames?
Nikhil (sec-eng): draft list: internal_user_id, host_internal_host, shard_key, service_token_id, ephemeral_kv_refs. Keep actor.name and actor.type, but actor.id becomes hashed id for member_view.
Sam (legal): make sure hashed ids are non-reversible and documented. also need export consent language for customers receiving audit exports.
Alex (eng-platform): question on scoped tokens: should a scoped token with "audit:read:org" be treated same as admin? or we gate by role mapping?
Nikhil (sec-eng): we should require mapping: scoped token + org_role==admin => admin_view. scoped token w/out admin role => member_view. That prevents token-only escalation.
Chris (eng-sre): what about lookup performance for hash mapping? we need deterministic mapping for cross-export correlation. We can use HMAC with org-specific salt from KMS.
Nikhil (sec-eng): exactly. plan: HMAC(id, KMS/org-salt) => public_actor_id. KMS access audited; salt rotates quarterly. Document rotation effects in release notes.
Maria (product): customers may ask to see original ids for forensics. propose a privileged rehydrate job that requires legal + customer approval (and full KMS audit). Any objections?
Sam (legal): ok with rehydrate if we have an approval workflow + audit trail. add additional step: customer signs scope doc.
Alex (eng-platform): implementation notes: we need a schema field metadata.visibility = [internal|admin|member] and an export transform that strips/annotates fields accordingly. Example event snippet: ```json
{
  "event_type":"token.create",
  "actor":{ "name":"deploy-bot", "type":"service", "id":"<HMAC:...>", "visibility":"member" },
  "meta":{ "service_token_id":"REDACTED:internal" }
}
```
Nikhil (sec-eng): nice. also need to surface to customers which export version they got and the applied visibility policy. put export_version + visibility_policy_id into header.
Chris (eng-sre): raising an ops concern: when we roll out schema changes, old parsers will break. versioning required and grace period for both export and ingest.
Maria (product): agreed. product will own communication plan and a 30-day deprecation period for old export schemas.
Alex (eng-platform): KMS integration: use seals per-org. ensure low-latency HMAC keys cached in KMS proxy. auditbot will log every key use.
AuditBot: Key use logged: org=acme-corp, key_id=k-789, action=derive_hmac, ts=1719504350
Nikhil (sec-eng): vuln triage note: if someone can request export and specify export_type=internal while not authorized, we must deny early in the API layer. add policy check in the export endpoint.
Chris (eng-sre): will add a policy gate in gateway with a metric for denied attempts.
Maria (product): next steps: Nikhil to produce a short RFC with schema diffs + mapping table, Alex to sketch KMS proxy changes, Chris to estimate perf & ops cost, Sam to outline legal checklist.
Nikhil (sec-eng): I'll draft RFC by EOD tomorrow and include example payloads. tagging @Maria @Alex @Chris @Sam for review. :+1:
Maria (product): thanks — pushed to review when ready. :eyes: 
Alex (eng-platform): ack.
Chris (eng-sre): ack.
